Rotated page, very tight crop: the ink spans rows 15-496 / cols 7-505, and exactly two circuit wires leave the drawing at the top (the left rail at x~95 and the lead of Resistor 3 at x~387) and exactly two at the bottom (the left rail at x~119 and the lead of Inductor 5 at x~392-405). The long straight lines at x~7-27 and x~487-505 are the notebook page rules, not wires.
Net map: 0 = the left rail, the only ground node: it runs unbroken from the top edge (x~95) down to the bottom edge (x~119), takes the T at (111,350) that carries the horizontal running right into the left lead of I-AC 0 (2cos4t A), and takes the GND 6 lead T-ing in at (116,408) (GND is drawn rotated, bars around x 48-107, lead running right). n1 = the right column at the junction dot (393,311): right lead of I-AC 0, bottom plate lead of Capacitor 2 (0.5 F) coming down from y~203, and the top lead of Inductor 5 (2 H) going down to y~399. n2 = right column between the bottom of Resistor 3 (1 ohm) at y~103 and the top plate of Capacitor 2 at y~184. n3 = top lead of Resistor 3 leaving the top edge at x~387 to one terminal of V-AC 1. n4 = bottom lead of Inductor 5 leaving the bottom edge at x~400 to one terminal of Resistor 4.
Circuit as read: V-AC in series with the 1 ohm resistor charging the 0.5 F cap into node n1, the 2cos4t A source injecting into n1 from ground, and the 2 H inductor returning through the off-frame resistor to ground. Every part has a return path.
OFF-FRAME COMPONENTS (not visible in the image at all):
 - V-AC 1, bbox centre (255.0,-55.7) spanning x~216-294 ABOVE the top edge. The only two wires crossing the top edge are the left rail (x~95, net 0) and Resistor 3's top lead (x~387, net n3), and the source sits horizontally between them. Inferred: terminal 0 = the lead facing left -> 0, terminal 1 = the lead facing right -> n3. V-AC has no polarity marks anyway and 2-terminal order is not metric-relevant.
 - Resistor 4, bbox centre (272.7,625.8) spanning x~221-325 BELOW the bottom edge. The only two wires crossing the bottom edge are the left rail (x~119, net 0) and Inductor 5's bottom lead (x~392-405, net n4), and the resistor sits horizontally between them. Inferred: terminal 0 = left -> 0, terminal 1 = right -> n4. Without it the 2 H inductor and the whole right column would have no return to ground.
 - Resistor 3 is only partly visible (bbox y -13.8..103): its zigzag body is in frame, its top lead is cut off. Top terminal = n3 (to V-AC 1), bottom terminal = n2 (to the capacitor). Inductor 5 is likewise clipped at the bottom (bbox y 398.6..512.8); top = n1, bottom = n4.
 Neither off-frame part is marked unconnected - they are outside the crop, not dangling.
Judgment calls: (a) (393,311) is a genuine junction - at 8x the crossing carries a distinct ink blob and the vertical continues both above and below, so I-AC's right lead, the capacitor and the inductor are one node; (b) (111,350) is a corner-plus-continuation: the left rail keeps going down past the point where the horizontal leaves, verified at 8x, so the rail above and below the horizontal is one net; (c) the GND lead meets the rail at (116,408) as a plain T = junction, which is what makes the whole left rail net 0; (d) two-terminal order: verticals (Resistor 3, Capacitor 2, Inductor 5) listed top-then-bottom, horizontals (I-AC 0 and the two off-frame parts) left-then-right; the I-AC arrow points right.
